scope: Every Characters row with more than one explicitly recorded reading; no missing readings are added.
policy: Editorial review requested by the project owner. Exact imported rows and existing reviewed meanings remain intact. Separate meanings only where cited dictionaries support the exact readings; identical meanings remain grouped. Explicit source-reviewed pronunciation choices are applied only to unchanged original tuples and disclose their original readings and source disagreement. Historical and regional context remains independent of etymology and geometry.

cases.note: This card uses dictionary-attested nì / nǐ as an explicit editorial pronunciation choice. The original Unihan ní / nǐ remains preserved: Unicode’s 2023 proposal records a change from nì to ní, whereas CC-CEDICT and Han Dian attach the dialectal I/we/my/our senses to nì. Taiwan MOE identifies nǐ as an old variant meaning you. This is a documented source disagreement, not a claim that Unihan has a typo. Audio uses Mandarin syllables, not a recording of Shanghai dialect speech.
ccCedictEntries: 伲 伲 [ni3] /variant of 你[ni3]/
伲 伲 [ni4] /(dialect) I/my/we/our/

cases.note: This card uses dictionary-attested pōu / pǒu. CC-CEDICT explicitly identifies pǒu as the Taiwan pronunciation; Taiwan MOE lists pǒu with pōu as an alternate, and CNS11643 records both. They share the cut-open, split and analyze meanings, so the card groups them with separate speakers. The original imported pōu / pǒ remains preserved as source provenance. The restored u changes the syllable: pǒu uses the existing pou3 recording, never the original po3 recording. Mainland pronunciation guidance gives 解剖 as jiě pōu, not jiě pāo; Taiwan MOE independently records jiě pǒu.
